Read Before Your Next Show!  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ 

Hey Dave,

Trade shows are expensive, and it can be hard to know if they're "worth it.".

Booth fees, travel, samples, signage, time away from production and your family.... It all adds up.

If you're headed to 

**Fancy Food or The Good Food Mercantile later this month, or are already planning for Newtopia Now or SuperZoo,
or an ECRM session** later this summer.. 

**Let's make sure you've got a clear return on your investment.**

I recently taught my 

**Trade Show Success Formula** to over 300 CPG founders, and I want to recap the key lessons.

Here are the Cliffs Notes:

Step One: Craft Your WHYs

Two questions you must answer before you even pack your samples:

**1. Why are YOU going?** (Be specific. "To get more sales" isn't clear enough.)

**Get clear on this so that you know how to prioritize your time.** Is the goal to find a new distributor? Go to the panel on distribution. Is the goal to land a new chain account? Prioritize being at your booth. Just want to network and have fun? Ditch the booth and go to the afterparties. You do you. Just know that without a clear goal, you try to do 

**all the things** and end up spread too thin, exhausted, and feeling like you *need* to cram in all in.

**2. Why should a buyer care?** (Hint: it's not just because your product is
"delicious.")

Buyers say yes when your product helps 

**them** hit 

**their** category goals like margin or sales. If you can't articulate that, the buyer keeps on walking by, so spend time now figuring it out so your sales pitch stands out across the booth. 

Step Two: Prep Your P's

**You've got one shot to come across as a legit, low-maintenance vendor they can trust.** That means being dialed on:

* 

**Product** (What you're selling and which SKUs you lead with)

* 

**Pricing** (Comparables, incentives, margins)

* 

**Placement** (Dream accounts, shelf strategy, merchandising ideas)

* 

**Purchasing** (How they order and reorder. Make it easy to say yes.)

* 

**Promotion** (Your plan to move product 

**off** their shelves)

* 

**Plus: Physical Setup -** If they won't stop at your booth, shoppers won't stop at the shelf either.

We get more into these 5 P's in Retail Ready®, but you've got the high level roadmap right here. 

Step Three: Follow Up
(Relentlessly)

If you only remember one thing from this email, let it be this:

**The squeaky wheel gets the shelf space.**

Most founders don't lose the sale because their product wasn't good enough. They lose it because they didn't follow up enough to stay top of mind.

**Write those post-show sales emails before you go, while you've got the energy**. Send them consistently after. Keep the door open until you get a clear yes or no.

Buyers are swamped. Help them remember you by staying at the top of their inbox.

It's time to ask yourself: "Am I headed to this show with confidence on why I'm there, clarity on what makes it "worth it" as I head home, and a plan to follow up within 3 weeks after the show?"

If not, figure that out now. You've already invested so much by paying to attend, taking the time to go, and expending a LOT of energy once there. You deserve to make this show worth it.

Rooting for you,
Alli

They are a direct link to the people, their culture, and their way of life and that’s why I chose to present this dish at the James Beard Foundation dinner (See below). While steadily gaining popularity here with gourmands and lovers of Italian foods, caciocavallo ranks among the most popular cheeses in Italy, along with Parmigiano, pecorino, and mozzarella. The process of making caciocavallo is a time-honored craft. Authentic caciocavallo is made from the milk of the Podolico cow found only in the Apennine Mountains between Basilicata and Calabria, and now at risk of extinction. These are very special cows, sturdy enough to withstand the rugged terrain and climate, yet gentle enough to have become the farmers’ best friend for millennia. I have never seen anyone make better caciocavallo than my late father, Biagio. He was a maestro at shaping the cheese, and I was always impressed at the many different shapes he could quickly create. Today, the tradition lives on with my brother Antonio, who still raises Podolico cows and who for three months out of every year continues to make wonderful caciocavallo. Work with your hands to form dough. Dust a work surface with the remaining flour and place the dough on top. Knead dough for about 10 minutes, incorporating a little extra flour as needed until it is smooth and pliable. To test if the dough is dry enough, poke it with a finger. If your finger is dry, you are ready to proceed. If your finger is sticky, add more flour, a bit at a time, and continue to knead the dough. When ready, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 30 minutes. To make the filling Combine the caciocavallo, egg, and ricotta in a medium bowl. Mixing very slowly with a wooden spoon, gently incorporate the ingredients. To shape the ravioli Set rollers of a pasta machine at the widest opening. Take an egg-size piece of dough while keeping the remaining dough covered with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel. Flatten the piece of dough, dust it with flour, and fold it in half. This profile was written by the Food Business Review research and editorial team based on insights from an interview with Michael Potter, President and research. Eden Foods - Built on Soil, Sustained by Principle In an industry often defined by scale, speed, and market pursuing a quieter, more deliberate ambition: purity. Under the stewardship of Michael Potter, the company’s trajectory reflects not a race against competitors, but a sustained commitment to redefining what food should be at its most fundamental level. That distinction, subtle yet profound, shapes every dimension of Eden Foods’ philosophy, from sourcing and production to its broader role within the organic movement. The origins of the company are neither corporate nor strategic in the conventional sense. They are deeply personal. In the late 1960s, a small group of young adults in Ann Arbor, Michigan, became increasingly aware of the growing adulteration of commercial food. Their concern was not abstract. It was immediate and intimate, tied to their own lives and the families they hoped to build. As Potter explains, “the goal was to get good food for our children.” What began as a self-centered pursuit of unadulterated nourishment gradually evolved into a broader ethos, one that now extends to communities, consumers, and future generations. The evolution has not diluted the company’s core objective. If anything, it has sharpened it. Eden Foods’ identity remains anchored in the pursuit of purity, a principle that has endured through decades of industry transformation. Over time, the company has expanded its capabilities, refined its sourcing networks, and broadened its product portfolio. Yet the central question, what constitutes truly good food, has remained unchanged. It is a question that Eden Foods answers not through marketing narratives, but through a disciplined, principle-driven approach to agriculture and production. Locked on Long-Term Viability Central to that approach is a reframing of what organic means. While regulatory frameworks often define organic certification through documentation and compliance, Eden Foods operates from a more foundational perspective. Its definition is rooted in the vitality of the soil. For the company, organic agriculture is not merely the absence of synthetic inputs; it is the presence of life. The distinction is critical. Soil, in this context, is not an inert medium but a living system, and its health directly determines the quality of the food it produces. This emphasis on soil vitality informs every aspect of Eden Foods’ sourcing strategy. The company prioritizes relationships with growers who share its long-term vision, often working with the same farms across multiple generations. These partnerships are not transactional. They are developmental, requiring patience, investment, and a shared understanding of the challenges inherent in organic farming. Transitioning land from conventional to organic practices, for instance, is not a simple procedural shift. It is a multi-year process of restoration, during which the soil must recover from years of chemical exposure and gradually rebuild its biological complexity. “We try to provide the best quality, the purest food we possibly can, and good information about it.” The results of that process are cumulative. As soil health improves, so do crop yields, flavor profiles, and nutritional density. This progression underscores a key belief within Eden Foods: that the integrity of food begins long before it is harvested. It begins in the soil, in the unseen ecosystem that sustains plant life. This perspective also explains the company’s skepticism toward shortcuts, whether in agriculture or in broader industry practices. Quick gains, in Eden’s view, often come at the expense of long-term viability. Committed to Doing Food Correctly The company’s philosophy extends to its stance on competition. Si no puede visualizar bien este boletín haga clic AQUÍLima, miércoles 03 de junio del 2026 Director General: Carlos Bernuy  El Taj Hessischer Hof, marca de India, abre sus puertas en FrankfurtIndian Hotels Company (IHCL), la mayor empresa hotelera de la India, anunció hoy la inauguración del Taj Hessischer Hof Frankfurt, lo que marca la entrada de la marca en Europa continental.
Leer más Pismo Beach nombrada la mejor playa de California por USA TODAY 10Best
Pismo Beach, California, ha sido elegida la mejor playa de California en los premios USA TODAY 10Best Readers’ Choice Awards 2026. Este reconocimiento marca la tercera vez que Pismo Beach obtiene el primer puesto a nivel nacional en los premios USA TODAY 10Best, tras haber sido nombrada mejor ciudad costera pequeña en 2025 y 2026.
Leer más
Princess Cruises anuncia la temporada europea más grande para el 2028
Princess Cruises presenta su temporada europea más extensa para 2028, con 291 salidas en 150 itinerarios únicos a bordo de seis barcos que navegarán por el norte de Europa, el Mediterráneo y en viajes transatlánticos.
Leer másUruguay se fortalece en el mercado peruano con eventos deportivos y experiencias premium
Uruguay continúa consolidándose como uno de los destinos más atractivos y versátiles de Sudamérica para el mercado peruano, combinando grandes eventos deportivos internacionales con experiencias vinculadas a la naturaleza, la gastronomía, el bienestar y el turismo premium. Bajo el lema “Uruguay: Más de lo que imaginas”, la Cámara Uruguaya de Turismo (CAMTUR) en conjunto con el Ministerio de Turismo de Uruguay (MINTUR) organizaron una presentación para operadores turísticos en Lima, Perú.
Leer más
GUEXT 2026 lanza su Programa de Compradores Internacionales
GUEXT, el Salón Internacional de Proveedores y Servicios para el sector Hospitality organizado por IFEMA MADRID junto a FELAC, la Federación Española de Asociaciones de Fabricantes de Maquinaria para Hostelería, Colectividades e Industrias Afines, anuncia el lanzamiento del GUEXT Hosted Buyers del 15 al 17 de octubre.
Leer más
Kansas City y Dallas disparan las búsquedas de hospedajes de los argentinos
Donde hay una pelota hay un argentino y en el mes de junio las búsquedas de alojamiento en Kansas City y Dallas se dispararon a niveles extraordinarios. Tal es así que Kansas City (con fechas de check-in 14 de junio y check-out 17 de junio) registra un incremento de búsquedas de hospedajes por parte de argentinos del 300% en comparación con las mismas fechas en 2025. Además, los argentinos se ubican entre las diez nacionalidades que más buscaron hospedajes para las fechas mencionadas en la ciudad de Kansas City.
Leer másAeroméxico y ViX ofrecerán WiFi gratuito y fútbol en vivo a bordo
Aeroméxico ha anunciado una colaboración junto a la plataforma de streaming ViX. Del 11 de junio al 31 de julio, los pasajeros de vuelos seleccionados podrán disfrutar de conectividad inalámbrica gratuita para acceder al catálogo de la plataforma, incluyendo las transmisiones de los torneos de fútbol más esperados del verano.
Leer más The Westerly abre con experiencia elevada en Hilton Aruba Caribbean Resort
Hilton Aruba Caribbean Resort & Casino celebró la inauguración oficial de The Westerly, dando paso a una propuesta sofisticada de hospitalidad elevada en el icónico resort de Palm Beach. Este debut marca una evolución significativa para la propiedad, introduciendo una experiencia más íntima para los huéspedes que combina diseño contemporáneo, servicio personalizado, espacios sociales dinámicos y la belleza natural de Aruba. El hito fue conmemorado con un evento al que asistieron representantes de la compañía, líderes de Hilton, funcionarios gubernamentales y socios clave del proyecto.

Sube turismo internacional en España en visitas e ingresosEl desarrollo sostenido del turismo internacional en España alcanzó ingresos por 36 mil 700 millones de euros y visitas en abril de 9,1 millones de viajeros, dijo una fuente oficial.
Leer más ONU Turismo registra 307 millones de viajeros en cuatrimestre
La oficina central de ONU Turismo, con sede en Madrid, informó hoy que durante el primer cuatrimestre del año, 307 millones de personas viajaron por el mundo.
Leer másManzanillo cierra temporada de cruceros con más de 57 mil visitantes
La Temporada de Cruceros 2025-2026 en Manzanillo concluyó de manera exitosa con un registro de 57 mil 539 viajeros y la llegada de 17 embarcaciones entre septiembre de 2025 y mayo de 2026, colocando al puerto colimense como uno de los principales puntos de llegada de turistas del Pacífico mexicano.

Conflicto en Oriente Medio amenaza con restar 23 millones de turistas a la región
El recrudecimiento de la crisis geopolítica en Oriente Medio, vinculada a las hostilidades bélicas con Irán, amenaza con paralizar de forma inmediata la progresión de uno de los mercados de mayor dinamismo para la industria de los viajes
